record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.original_question: Develop a theory of geometric conditions that define strata for tensegrity configuration spaces in the multidimensional case, beyond the planar setting.

evidence.quote: There is almost nothing known in multidimensional case.
Problem 9 Develop theory of geometric conditions for strata in multidimensional case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite graph with n vertices and let d ≥ 3 be an integer. A configuration of G in R^d is a map p : V → R^d. A tensegrity (or self-stress) on (G, p) is an assignment of weights w : E → R, one per edge, satisfying the equilibrium condition at every vertex v ∈ V:
  Σ_{u : {u,v} ∈ E} w_{uv} (p(u) − p(v)) = 0.
The configuration space of G in R^d is the space of all maps p : V → R^d (up to a chosen equivalence, e.g. affine or Euclidean), and its tensegrity stratification is the decomposition according to the dimension (and combinatorial type) of the cone of self-stresses W(G, p). In the planar case d = 2, the strata of codimension 1 (and several higher codimension strata) admit explicit descriptions by classical projective geometric conditions on the points p(v) (expressible, for instance, through Cayley-algebra/meet–join operations, with conditions such as "six points lie on a conic" appearing for specific graphs).

Problem. Develop a systematic theory of geometric (projective/incidence) conditions that cut out the strata of the tensegrity stratification of the configuration space of an arbitrary graph G in R^d for d ≥ 3. In particular, for each combinatorial type of self-stress cone, give explicit geometric conditions on the configuration p : V → R^d that characterize membership in the corresponding stratum, generalizing the known planar descriptions to the multidimensional setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that geometric conditions defining strata of tensegrity configuration spaces are well-studied only in the planar case (via Cayley/meet-join expressions, conics, Pascal-type theorems). In dimensions d ≥ 3 the literature explicitly states that almost nothing is known, and no systematic theory of stratum-defining geometric conditions has been developed. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: Existing geometric/symbolic descriptions of tensegrity strata concentrate on the planar case.
